source.title: ScalingNote: Scaling up Retrievers with Large Language Models for Real-World Dense Retrieval
source.authors: Suyuan Huang; Chao Zhang; Yuan-Yuan Wu; Haoxin Zhang; Yuan Wang; Mao-Lin Wang; Shaosheng Cao; Tong Xu; Xiang-Yu Zhao; Zengchang Qin; Yan Gao; Yunhan Bai; Jun Fan; Yao Hu; En-Hong Chen

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some mathematical formatting, particularly the mixed-scaling equation, is garbled in the extracted text.
record.tranche_reason: The study fits power-law curves to a retrieval validation loss while varying retriever model size and training-data size. This tests scaling behavior conceptually, but uses a retrieval measure rather than held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The paper reports three scaling-law fits for contrastive entropy on a validation dataset. It also reports AUC and recall results for several training datasets and methods, but those method-comparison table entries are not fitted scaling-law results and are not included as rows here. The online A/B results concern an integrated retrieval system, not a measured language-model pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes pretrained Qwen2.5 LLMs (0.5B–7B) into dual-tower dense retrievers on industrial data. It fits power laws to validation contrastive entropy as model size and training-pair count vary. This is a new regime (contrastive fine-tuning for retrieval) with its own scaling result, so T3 fits better than T2. It bears mainly on V5 (fine-tuning/transfer) and partly on V6 (a downstream task improving predictably with scale). It says nothing on V1–V4 or V7 for pretraining loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors say their experiments verify a scaling law for LLM-based dense retrieval in their industrial setting. One correction: the claim that data-scaling benefits diminish near 10^8 pairs, and that model scaling then becomes more effective, is read off the fitted mixed law (Eq. 20). It was not observed in the scaling sweep, which used at most about 1M pairs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a power-law fitting approach for a related scaling question, but measures dense-retrieval validation contrastive entropy rather than held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy. It does not test compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling behavior is studied using a particular industrial training pipeline, a Small validation dataset, and contrastive entropy; the paper does not compare alternative fitting choices.
record.problems: The scaling-law sweep is conducted on one industrial retrieval setting and uses validation contrastive entropy rather than language-model pretraining loss. The mixed-fit equation is garbled in the extracted text. The paper does not report an out-of-sample extrapolation test or a sensitivity analysis of fitting choices.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 3 and 4 report AUC and recall results across methods and Small, Median, and Large training datasets; these method-comparison values were not extracted because they are not reported as fitted scaling-law results. Table 6 reports student-query-tower distillation results at different sizes, rather than the Stage-I scaling-law sweep. These appear in Sections 4.3–4.5 and Tables 3, 4, and 6.

untested.parts: Image/video models and repeated-data regimes are untested. Scale range is narrow (about 1 order of magnitude in N and in D), so the 'over several orders of magnitude' part is untested.

The study gives no mapping from pretraining loss to downstream performance and no range of downstream tasks. Only retrieval loss on one validation set is fitted; AUC and recall are not fitted against scale.
The authors use the mixed fit to reason about data near 1e8 pairs, but never check a fitted prediction against larger runs.

missing.what: AUC and recall for each method trained on Small (~0.9M), Median (~19.6M) and Large (~118M) pairs. All methods rise monotonically with data, e.g. ScalingDual R@1k 75.48→86.79→90.62. This is downstream gain with data scale over about two orders of magnitude.
Student query-tower size (8M, 29M, 86M) versus recall/AUC with a fixed 7B document tower. Gains shrink with size (R@50 49.56→54.57→54.91).

record.verdict_notes: Linking rows to V6 is borderline: the measure is a task-specific validation loss, not a downstream accuracy metric. The Table 3/4 data-scale trends would strengthen the V6 link if extracted. The scaling sweep is small (4 model sizes, data under one order of magnitude), so the high R² values carry limited weight. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The paper fits curves but does not report testing predictions from small runs against substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.
Tests one industrial dense-retrieval training setting; does not test image or video models, repeated-data training, or other transfer and fine-tuning regimes.
Measures retrieval validation contrastive entropy, not a range of general downstream tasks or downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss.
Does not systematically vary fitting method, parameter counting, training schedule, or data setup to compare resulting exponents; no reported departure from the fitted curves.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 series
rows.size_stated: 0.5B, 1.5B, 3B, and 7B; retriever parameter count is specified as non-embedding parameters
rows.stage_stated: LLM-based dense retriever trained on the Small training dataset
rows.operation_detail: Varied model size and fitted contrastive entropy on the Small validation dataset to a power law.
rows.measure: Contrastive entropy; fitted model-size scaling law
rows.note: The authors state that loss decreases as model size scales. The reported fit aggregates the Qwen2.5 size sweep.
rows.check: Value is correct. The fit rests on only four model sizes (0.5B–7B, about one order of magnitude) with three free parameters, so R²=0.9999 is weak evidence. Note that the models are different pretrained checkpoints, not a controlled size sweep.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 7B
rows.stage_stated: LLM-based dense retriever trained on the Small training dataset
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of training query-document pairs and fitted contrastive entropy to a power law.

conditions.value: D, number of training query-document pairs

rows.measure: Contrastive entropy; fitted data-size scaling law
rows.note: The body gives the equation; the extracted text does not give a readable R² for this fit.
rows.check: Figure 5(b) text gives R² = 0.9993 and exponent 0.142; the record says R² is unreadable. The data sweep spans only about 250K–1M training pairs, under one order of magnitude.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 series
rows.stage_stated: LLM-based dense retriever trained with varying model sizes and training-data sizes
rows.operation_detail: Varied model size and training-data size together and fitted validation contrastive entropy to a mixed scaling function.

conditions.value: N, number of non-embedding parameters; D, number of training query-document pairs

rows.measure: Contrastive entropy; mixed model-size and data-size scaling fit
rows.value: Mixed power-law fit in Eq. 20; the equation is garbled in the extracted text. R² = 0.9887.
rows.note: The authors report fitting the mixed scaling law, but the formula cannot be reliably reconstructed from the provided text.
rows.check: The equation is partly readable: terms (3.15e5/N)^0.12, (1.16e2/D), an exponent shown as 770, and +0.108; R²=0.9887. Exact form uncertain. Range is the same 4 sizes × up to ~1M pairs.

relationships.condition: Contrastive fine-tuning of Qwen2.5 0.5B–7B as dense retrievers on Xiaohongshu data, ≤1M training pairs
relationships.reason: Validation contrastive entropy fits a power law plus constant in N (R²=0.9999), in D (R²=0.9993) and jointly (R²=0.9887) (r1, r2, r3). Ranges are narrow.
relationships.display_finding: Contrastive entropy fitted power laws plus constants with R²=0.9999 for model size, 0.9993 for data size and 0.9887 jointly, over narrow ranges.

relationships.condition: Retrieval task loss of fine-tuned LLM retrievers on the Small validation set
relationships.reason: Retrieval loss falls smoothly and is well fitted by a power law in model size and data size (r1–r3). Only one task and one loss-type metric are measured.
relationships.display_finding: Retrieval loss decreases smoothly and fits a power law in model and data size on the single evaluated task.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The size, data, and mixed sweeps are reported to follow fitted power-law forms for retrieval validation contrastive entropy (r1–r3); this supports the form in this retrieval training regime only.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Retrieval validation contrastive entropy in the tested setting
reader_labels.reason: The measured retrieval loss decreases with model size and training-data size, and the authors report fitted scaling curves (r1–r3); this is evidence for predictable scaling of this retrieval metric, not general downstream-task performance.
